symptom.title: Correction without behavioral change
symptom.summary: An agent acknowledges a specific correction and then repeats the corrected behavior under comparable conditions.

observation.p: After receiving and acknowledging an applicable correction, the agent performs materially the same corrected action at least once more while that correction remains in force. The acknowledgment and later action are both observable in the episode or linked continuation.

how-to-recognize-it.p: Pair an acknowledged correction with the next relevant action in the transcript. A small classifier can flag repeated violations for review; exclude actions already in progress when the correction arrived.

lookalike.p: The later action falls outside the correction’s stated scope. It therefore lacks the applicable correction required by repeated violation.
A later applicable instruction changes the rule, or a higher-priority requirement displaces it. The original correction is no longer in force as required by repeated violation.
Execution logs show that the apparent recurrence was issued before the correction and acknowledgment. It is not a later action chosen after acknowledgment under repeated violation.

what-to-record.p: Record the episode identifier and date, task type, model/harness versions, the correction’s exact text and scope, its delivery and acknowledgment times, and each subsequent opportunity to apply it. Preserve later actions, intervening instructions, memory artifacts, and effective input where available. Include recurrence counts relative to relevant opportunities, user correction turns, elapsed delay, damaged or redone work, and whether behavior eventually changed. Distinguish missing context evidence from a demonstrated loss of the correction.

example.p: After being told to edit a source template rather than generated output, the agent acknowledges the correction but makes the next fix in the generated file. Comparing the correction with the diff identifies the recurrence. The next build overwrites that fix, leaving one unresolved defect and ten minutes of rework.

Claude Code issue #37847 lists eight shell-command recurrences after feedback was saved: four Python, two shell-loop, and two Node examples. The reporter compared saved memory and acknowledgments with later commands, describing repeated corrections and lost confidence in memory. Total time lost and the effective input to every invocation are not supplied.

After prohibiting edits to generated output, the user explicitly approves one emergency edit there. The transcript records that exception before the single edit, so the change does not violate a correction that remained in force for that action.
